blocks.raw:
<Tip>
Memory aid for schedules: **Completeness, Consistency, Coordination**. Every schedule must be complete (all columns filled), consistent internally (door marks match drawings), and coordinated with specifications and drawings. A missing door mark or hardware set is a red flag. Always verify schedule accuracy before sending to bidding or construction.
</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeCard mistake="Specifying different performance criteria in the schedule versus the specification. Example: window schedule specifies 'U-value 0.22' but Division 08 specification requires 'U-value 0.25 minimum.' This ambiguity creates disputes over which document controls." correction="The specification typically controls performance and acceptance criteria. The schedule should reference specification sections (e.g., 'See Division 08 for glazing requirements'). Never let schedule and specification criteria conflict. If they differ, the specification (Part 1: General) must clarify which takes precedence." />
